in_greek.name: Ξέρξης
in_greek.meaning: Ο Μέγας Βασιλεύς, ένδυναμος ή μέγας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ξέρξης είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του περσικού ονόματος Khshayarsha, που σημαίνει 'ο μεγάλος βασιλιάς' ή 'ένδυναμος'. Ο Ξέρξης Α' ήταν ο πιο γνωστός βασιλιάς με αυτό το όνομα, που κυβέρνησε την Περσία τον 5ο αιώνα π.Χ.

in_latin.name: Xerxes
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Xerxes originem habet persicam, significans 'regem magnum' vel 'validum'. Xerxes I, rex Persiae, fuit rex illustris, qui quinto saeculo ante Christum regnavit. Nomen etiam in Scripturis, libro Ezrae, invenitur.

in_english.name: Xerxes
in_english.meaning: The Great King, powerful or large
in_english.long_meaning: The name Xerxes originates from the Persian Khshayarsha, meaning 'the great king' or 'powerful'. Xerxes I was a famous king of Persia who ruled in the 5th century BC. The name appears in the Bible, in the book of Ezra, referring to the same king. The name symbolizes strength and grandeur, reflecting the king's powerful reign and legacy.

biblical_reference.note: King Xerxes I, also known as Ahasuerus, is mentioned in the book of Ezra.

data.cultural_impact: In Persian culture, Xerxes was a legendary king who was known for his immense wealth and power. He is most famous for leading a large-scale invasion of Greece in 480 BC, which is depicted in the historical texts of both Greece and Persia. This military campaign is known as the Second Persian Invasion of Greece or the Greco-Persian Wars, and it greatly impacted Western civilization by introducing new cultural influences such as Persian architecture and art.
data.spiritual_significance: King Xerxes I, as mentioned in the book of Esther, ruled during a time when the Jews in Persia were facing severe persecution. However, Esther, a Jewish queen, successfully pleaded for their lives and secured their freedom, which is a significant reminder of the protection and deliverance offered by God during difficult times. The name Xerxes can serve as a reminder of the power and authority of God, who rules over all things and can bring redemption and triumph out of adversity. Additionally, the figure of Esther can inspire us to courageously stand up for our beliefs and to trust in God's providence, even when facing seemingly insurmountable challenges.

historical_references.reference: Xerxes I, also known as Xerxes the Great, was a king of the Achaemenid Empire (521-486 BC) who is best known for leading a large invasion of Greece. This invasion was described in detail by the ancient Greek historian Ctesias in his work 'The History of Persia'. In 480 BC, Xerxes amassed a vast army and fleet, believed to be over 100,000 men and 1,200 ships respectively, and set out to conquer Greece. The Greeks, under the leadership of Leonides of Sparta, held the pass of Thermopylae and held out against the Persian forces for several days, despite being vastly outnumbered. The encounter ended with a Persian victory, but at great cost, and is considered a pivotal moment in the war.
historical_references.context: Achaemenid Empire, Persian invasion of Greece

historical_references.reference: Xerxes II, also known as Xerxes the Young, was a king of the Achaemenid Empire (486-465 BC) who succeeded his father, Xerxes I. His reign was marked by conflicts with Egypt and Greece. In 460 BC, there was an uprising in Egypt, and Egypt's satrap (governor) Inaros rebelled against the Persian rule. Xerxes sent an army under the command of Megabyzus to put down the rebellion, but the Egyptian forces, aided by Greek mercenaries and Athenian ships, were able to repel the invasion. This marked the last major Persian attempt to conquer Egypt, and the beginning of the end of Persian hegemony in the eastern Mediterranean.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Xerxes continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Xerxes in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Xerxes, which means "King, ruler". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Xerxes was a Persian king known for his grandeur and military might. In a Christian context, Xerxes could symbolize the worldly power and ambition that Christians are called to resist in their spiritual journey. His name serves as a reminder to value inner strength and humility over worldly achievements.
